title: Why Financial Document Processing Is Still Broken
summary: Traditional document processing fails exactly where financial services needs it most. | Pulse AI
body_text: Most financial services firms have invested heavily in document AI over the past few years. The promise is compelling: automate the tedious work of extracting data from CIMs, financial statements, and research reports so analysts can focus on higher-value analysis. But there's a gap between the demo and reality. The next generation of document AI works well on clean, simple documents. The issue is financial documents are neither clean nor simple. They combine complex table structures, dense numerical data, and visual elements in ways that push the current models beyond their designed capabilities. At Pulse, we’ve been testing document AI systems across thousands of financial documents to understand where the technology breaks down. We tested the latest language models, open source solutions, and enterprise platforms. The pattern is consistent: systems that achieve 90%+ accuracy on standard text drop to 70-80% accuracy on the structured financial data that drives analytical decisions. The gap isn't about character recognition. It's about understanding the structural relationships that make financial documents meaningful. The Table Structure Problem Financial documents are built around complex table relationships that standard OCR systems simply don't understand. Unlike simple invoices or contracts, financial statements use nested hierarchies where the structure itself carries meaning. Take a typical quarterly earnings breakdown. You might have revenue split by geography, then by business unit, then by product line, with subtotals and percentages at each level. Traditional systems process each cell independently, completely losing the relationships that make the data meaningful. We've seen systems correctly extract every individual number from a complex P&L while completely scrambling which numbers belong to which categories. The raw data is perfect, but the structure that makes it useful disappears entirely. This isn't a character recognition problem. It's an architectural limitation of systems designed for simpler document types. Pulse’s approach to this is via extremely granular bounding box detection and a suite of heuristic algorithms that determine when to merge cells. Chart and Graph Blindness Modern financial documents rely heavily on visual elements to communicate key insights. Revenue trends, market share breakdowns, geographic distributions, growth trajectories. These aren't decorative. They often contain the most important analytical insights in the entire document. Traditional document AI either ignores charts completely or tries to extract text from legends and labels, missing the actual data relationships entirely. We tested this systematically across hundreds of CIMs and financial presentations. Chart-based insights, which often represent 40-60% of the analytical value in these documents, simply disappear during processing. Teams end up manually recreating analyses that should have been automated. The Precision Tax Financial analysis operates with precision requirements that don't exist in other industries. A small OCR error in a legal contract might require manual correction. The same error in financial data can cascade through interconnected calculations, creating systematic analytical distortions. Currency and decimal handling represents a particular failure mode. Systems that reliably process $ 1,234.56 in invoices start making errors when the same format appears in dense financial tables with varying fonts and formatting. We've observed systematic decimal shifting where $ 1,234.56 becomes $ 12,345.6 or currency markers disappear entirely. Percentage processing creates similar cascading problems. Growth rates, margins, and ownership percentages appear in dozens of different formats across financial documents, and traditional systems handle them inconsistently. ‍ The downstream impact compounds. A 1% error in extracting a key financial metric can shift valuation models by 10-20%. When you're processing hundreds of documents for portfolio analysis or market research, these errors accumulate into systematic analytical bias. The Real Estate Challenge In our experience dealing with thousands of different document layouts, real estate financial documents represent the absolute limit of document complexity. Rent rolls, operating statements, and property-level financial reports, to be specific. These combine dense numerical data with complex formatting in ways that break every traditional processing system we've tested. A typical institutional property rent roll contains 20+ interconnected columns: tenant information, lease terms, base rent, escalations, percentage rent, expense recoveries, renewal probabilities. Traditional AI processes these as independent data points, completely losing the economic relationships that define property performance. We've worked with several REITs on their document processing workflows. The consistent pattern we observe before they try Pulse is that traditional systems extract most of the raw data correctly but lose the analytical context. The Enterprise Workaround Problem Most financial services firms have developed elaborate workarounds for these limitations rather than solving them directly. The result is document processing workflows that are more complex and time-consuming than manual processes, while still requiring extensive manual verification. Hybrid processing chains where documents get run through multiple systems, with humans filling gaps and correcting errors. The automation savings get consumed by coordination overhead. Extensive verification protocols where analysts manually check all extracted financial data before using it in models. This eliminates the time savings from automation while adding verification work that didn't exist in manual processes. Selective automation where firms only automate the simplest document types, manually processing anything complex. This creates systematic bottlenecks where the documents that take longest to process manually are the same ones that can't be automated. ‍ Financial services firms are investing heavily in document AI based on demonstrations using simple examples. But real enterprise workflows involve complex document types where current technology doesn't work reliably. Internal tool development projects that assume reliable document extraction are building on unstable foundations. Firms focusing on semantic search systems can't accurately process CIMs due to errors in the ingestion step. Analytics platforms built from the ground up routinely miss chart-based insights. The firms that acknowledge these limitations and build purpose-built solutions will have systematic advantages over those that continue layering workarounds onto inadequate technology. The financial services industry needs document processing technology built specifically for the structural complexity and precision requirements of financial documents. Current solutions work well for standard business documents but fail systematically on the complex financial structures that drive investment and analytical decisions. ‍ This isn't about replacing human analysts. It's about giving them reliable automation for the document processing work that currently consumes 30-40% of their time while producing unreliable results. — We're working with several of the largest financial institutions to solve document processing for complex financial documents. Want to see how purpose-built systems compare to your current solutions? We can run direct comparisons on your document types.

Why onboarding a vendor isn't the same as approving a one-off purchase A one-off purchase usually has a value and vendor already defined. Onboarding a new vendor, on the other hand, generally involves comparing proposals, negotiating terms, and only then formalizing the decision — a process with more steps and more people involved. title: What Paper Records Really Cost a School District
summary: The copier contract is the smallest part of what paper costs a district. A look at where the real expense hides, and how to build a budget case for…
body_text: Every district has a room like this. Maybe it is a converted classroom behind the main office. Maybe it is a basement with a dehumidifier running in the corner, or a rented storage unit across town that shows up on a monthly invoice nobody questions. Inside are the cume folders, the special ed files, the personnel records going back to administrators who retired before anyone currently in the building was hired. Ask what that room costs and you will probably get a number from the copier contract. Paper, toner, service calls. That is not the expensive part. The registrar problem In August, a family moves into the district. The registrar needs the incoming student's file from their previous district, and a former student who just got into a nursing program needs a transcript from 2011, and there is a new bus driver whose paperwork has to go somewhere. On paper, each of those is a trip. Not a metaphorical trip, an actual walk to a cabinet, a search through a drawer, a photocopy, a walk back. Some of them are two trips because the file was not where it should have been. Occasionally one of them is a forty-minute problem because a folder got put back in the wrong year and now three people are looking for it. None of this is dramatic. That is the issue. It is fifteen minutes here and ten minutes there, spread across the registrar, the special education secretary, the HR generalist, and the front office aide, and it never gets logged anywhere. There is no line item called "staff time spent walking to filing cabinets," so it has never once come up in a budget discussion. It adds up to real money. Bloomington Public School District 87 timed their student record transfers before they digitized and found the process took up to ten minutes per student, counting the gathering, the review, the scanning, and the emailing. Afterward the same transfer ran in under thirty seconds. That is one workflow out of a dozen. If you want a number for your own district, pick your worst process and have someone time five instances of it. Multiply by how many you handle a year. Put your loaded hourly rate against the total. It is usually a bigger figure than people expect, and unlike most budget arguments, it is yours rather than a vendor's. Retention schedules are much harder to follow on paper Districts are not short on records obligations. FERPA governs how student information is safeguarded and prohibits the destruction of records while a request to inspect them is pending, as covered in the Department of Education's guidance on data retention and destruction . Special education files add another layer: 34 CFR 300.624 requires districts to notify parents when personally identifiable information is no longer needed for services and to destroy it if the parent requests it. Most of the day-to-day detail, though, comes from the state. Ohio districts work from a retention schedule approved by their records commission, the State Archives, and the Auditor of State, and the Ohio History Connection publishes a model schedule for school districts to build from. Other states run something similar. Now think about what following one of those schedules actually requires when the records are on paper. The schedule says a given record series gets destroyed after six years, or after audit, or after a student turns a certain age. Executing that means a person physically pulling the right folders out of the right drawers on the right timeline, in every building, every year, and documenting that they did it. Almost nobody does this. What happens instead is that districts fall behind, decide it is safer to keep everything, and end up storing forty years of records under a schedule that says they should be storing six. Then an auditor asks about it, or a public records request lands, and the response takes three weeks, and the gap becomes visible. Going digital does not change the obligation. It changes whether you can realistically meet it, because retention rules can run against records that are actually indexed instead of against a room. The room is worth something Space is the cost most people can see and still somehow discount. A five-drawer cabinet needs roughly sixteen square feet once you count the clearance to open it, and no district has just one. Whether that matter depends on your building. In a district with flat enrollment and spare space, reclaiming a storage room is nice but not urgent. In a district that is running a program out of a repurposed closet, or paying for offsite storage every month, or planning a levy partly around space constraints, it is a live argument. Worth knowing which one you are before you bring it up. The one that is hard to think about Paper can be destroyed all at once. A pipe breaks over a long weekend, or a roof fails, and decades of files are gone with nothing behind them. The odds in any given year are small. The problem is what it looks like afterward: former students who cannot get transcripts, records requests you cannot answer, retention requirements you cannot demonstrate compliance with because the evidence no longer exists. It is not a recoverable situation the way most facilities problems are. Districts already carry insurance against this category of risk everywhere else on campus. Records tend to be the exception, mostly because nobody has framed them as an asset. Where this usually stalls The reason records digitization dies in budget season is rarely that people disagree about the value. It is that the request shows up as a technology line item and lands next to devices, network upgrades, and instructional software, which is a fight it will lose most years. It is better positioned as operations and risk. The savings are in staff hours and facilities, and the exposure is compliance and continuity, none of which competes with a Chromebook refresh. The other thing that helps is scope. You do not have to do the whole district at once, and districts that get approval usually do not. They pick one series, often inactive student records or special ed files, and start there. It turns an intimidating capital ask into something a business official can slot into an existing budget without a board conversation. If you are thinking about where to start, we are happy to talk through what a first phase would look like for a district your size. Learn more about YellowFolder by Intellinetics .

title: Industry-Changing 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act Becomes Law
summary: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act became law July 11 without President Trump's signature. Here's what the landmark bipartisan housing bill means for manufactured housing, homebuyers, and the nation's 4-million-home shortage
body_text: Industry-Changing 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act Becomes Law Published On: July 13, 2026 • 3 min read • Landmark bipartisan legislation takes effect after president declines to sign or veto WASHINGTON, D.C. , July 11, 2026 — The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act automatically became law on Saturday , July 11, without President Donald Trump's signature, clearing a constitutional review period after the president announced he would neither sign nor veto the most sweeping federal housing legislation in decades. The bill passed both chambers by wide margins: 85-5 in the Senate on June 22 and 358-32 in the House on June 23. What the Law Does Allows qualifying manufactured homes to be built without a permanent chassis Modernizes FHA financing Exempts manufactured homes from restrictions aimed at large institutional investors Streamlines permitting and environmental reviews Directs federal regulators to study small-dollar mortgage barriers What This Means for Homebuyers More affordable housing options. Chassis-free designs can fit communities where manufactured homes were previously harder to place Potentially easier financing. Updated FHA loan limits and a study of lending barriers are designed to help more buyers qualify Possibility of faster, less costly approvals. Streamlined permitting and pre-approved building plans reduce time and expense before construction begins Fewer corporate competitors for starter homes. The provision applies to qualifying large institutional investors and restricts certain future purchases of single-family homes. Graphic courtesy of Manufactured Housing Institute (MHI) Boor: Real Change Happens at the State Level Bill Boor, President and CEO of Cavco Industries, applauded the bill’s passage into law, with an open take about both the opportunity and its limits. On the chassis reform provision, he said earlier this year: “Just removing that from the definition of a manufactured home opens up innovation opportunities for our industry: multi-story construction, ground-level installation, new placement options in urban and suburban markets. You start to see the opportunity for product innovation. And that opens up a whole new market opportunity for this industry.” He was equally consistent about what federal action alone cannot accomplish. “I always caution that a federal change won’t open up opportunities overnight. There’s a lot of work that has to happen at the state level once the definition is improved.” In this arena, Boor speaks from experience. He has testified mutliple times in front of Congressional committees advocating for the need to expand manufactured housing as a solution to the nation’s affordable housing crisis. In a LinkedIn post published the day Congress passed the legislation, Boor identified the law’s broader significance: “For the first time, Congress has explicitly recognized manufactured housing as part of the nation’s housing supply solution.” But he argued the harder work lies ahead – in state capitols, county offices and local planning meetings. “That is where housing opportunity becomes housing reality.” The nation’s housing shortage is estimated at approximately 4 million homes. The median price of an existing U.S. home reached $440,600 in June, according to the National Association of Realtors. As Boor put it: “All of these things are aimed toward more supply of factory-built housing – which is a supply the country needs at the lower end of the affordability discussion. They create real momentum. Not just for our company, but for the industry as a whole and hopeful homebuyers across America.” Shop Homes July 10, 2026 Jeff Williams, Cavco Regional Vice President Receives 2026 MHAO Goodman-Ross Award June 24, 2026 Congress Advances Major Housing Priorities and Manufactured Housing Reforms June 8, 2026 New Affordable Senior Housing Community Breaks Ground in Kissimmee, Florida June 2, 2026 Virginia Takes a Step Forward for Affordable Housing at Cavco’s Rocky Mount Facility you might also like Jeff Williams, Cavco Regional Vice President Receives 2026 MHAO Goodman-Ross Award Categories: Latest News Congress Advances Major Housing Priorities and Manufactured Housing Reforms Categories: Latest News New Affordable Senior Housing Community Breaks Ground in Kissimmee, Florida Categories: Latest News

title: Kapital FX: Optimizando el proceso de cambio de divisas
summary: Descubre Kapital FX, la solución para gestionar divisas con seguridad, agilidad y sin comisiones. Optimiza el tipo de cambio y lleva tu empresa a mercados internacionales.
body_text: En el entorno empresarial actual, la competitividad es abrumadora: cualquier organización tiene la capacidad de integrarse a los mercados globales. Más que la ubicación física, el factor que define la relevancia de una organización es su agilidad financiera internacional . Para competir con éxito, no basta con un producto de excelencia; es esencial dominar la gestión del capital mediante el FX (Foreign Exchange por sus siglas en inglés) . Con frecuencia, el cambio de divisas se percibe como un simple trámite administrativo o un costo inevitable. No obstante, en Kapital se reconoce que el FX es una herramienta estratégica clave. No se trata solo de convertir moneda local a extranjera, sino de aprovechar las dinámicas del mercado para transformar la volatilidad en una oportunidad de crecimiento. Por ello, Kapital ha desarrollado Kapital FX un sistema de cambio de divisas que permite que el flujo de capital entre países sea tan ágil como una transferencia local. Ya sea para pagar a proveedores en Asia o recibir pagos desde Estados Unidos, contar con una estrategia sólida en divisas puede marcar la diferencia entre mantener la operación o expandirse hacia nuevos mercados. Kapital FX: impulsa la rentabilidad empresarial Kapital FX es el servicio especializado de cambio de divisas diseñado para empresas nacionales y extranjeras que buscan eficiencia, seguridad y un acompañamiento experto. A diferencia de la banca tradicional, donde los procesos suelen ser rígidos y tardados, Kapital fusiona tecnología con una planeación cambiaria personalizada . La plataforma permite a las organizaciones comprar y vender divisas con absoluta fluidez, centrando la estrategia en dos pilares fundamentales: Pactación del tipo de cambio: La empresa elige el momento ideal para realizar la operación, asegurando condiciones competitivas que protegen la rentabilidad del negocio. Gestión multimoneda: Ya sea que se opere en dólares estadounidenses (USD), euros (EUR) u otras divisas de relevancia, el proceso garantiza que el capital de trabajo mantenga su dinamismo en todo momento. Operar con Kapital FX implica la eliminación de procesos ambiguos. El servicio cuenta con límites claros, disponibilidad confirmada y una estructura de cero comisiones por contratación . Representa la libertad de movilizar recursos al ritmo que la empresa exige, con el respaldo de un grupo financiero que comprende los desafíos del mercado global. Divisas: Alcance internacional para las empresas En Kapital FX, la diversificación constituye la base de una estrategia financiera sólida. Por ello, se dispone de un servicio que ofrece las divisas con mayor liquidez y relevancia en el comercio internacional. La plataforma no funciona solo como un puente hacia el dólar, sino como una ventana hacia las economías más influyentes del planeta. Mediante esta operativa, el equipo financiero de cada empresa puede gestionar transacciones en las siguientes denominaciones: Dólar estadounidense ( USD ) Euro ( EUR ) Libra esterlina ( GBP ) Yen japonés ( JPY ) Dólar canadiense ( CAD ) Franco suizo ( CHF ) Peso mexicano ( MXN ) Disponer de este abanico de divisas permite tomar decisiones con claridad y rapidez, aprovechando las variaciones del mercado para maximizar la rentabilidad de cada operación. ¿Cómo se define el tipo de cambio para una operación empresarial? El tipo de cambio se establece previamente, tomando en cuenta factores como el monto, la moneda involucrada y el momento en que se realizará la operación. Esto permite a la empresa disminuir su exposición a la volatilidad del mercado y operar con mayor certeza y control financiero. ¿Existen montos mínimos o máximos para operar divisas? Kapital FX se adapta al volumen de cada organización. Si bien existe una operativa estándar para montos frecuentes, las empresas que requieran movilizar capitales de mayor escala disponen de esquemas corporativos especializados y soluciones diseñadas a la medida de las necesidades transfronterizas. Características de Kapital FX La movilidad del capital internacional requiere una infraestructura que combine velocidad, transparencia y un cumplimiento regulatorio impecable. El servicio de Kapital FX, permite que las transferencias de divisas operen como el motor de expansión para la empresa, transformando la complejidad del envío de fondos al extranjero en un proceso lógico y eficiente. Las características que definen la operativa de Kapital FX son: 1. Fondos confirmados Antes de cada ejecución, el sistema realiza una validación de disponibilidad de recursos. Esto garantiza que la empresa cuente con la liquidez necesaria en la divisa seleccionada, asegurando que el beneficiario reciba los fondos de manera puntual y sin rechazos operativos. 2. Trazabilidad bancaria Cada transferencia genera un comprobante de operación inmediato. Esto permite al equipo financiero mantener un control contable riguroso y una conciliación bancaria precisa, facilitando el cumplimiento de las obligaciones fiscales y de auditoría exigidas por la normativa mexicana. 3. Seguridad institucional Operar transferencias con Kapital FX significa contar con el respaldo de un grupo financiero. Cada movimiento está blindado por protocolos de encriptación avanzada y supervisado bajo los estándares de la CNBV y el Banco de México . 4. Eficiencia en costos y cero comisiones Bajo una política de transparencia, las transferencias dentro del ecosistema Kapital FX destacan por la ausencia de comisiones de contratación. La empresa puede movilizar recursos basándose en un tipo de cambio pactado y competitivo, optimizando el capital de trabajo. 5. Asesoría en la ejecución A diferencia de los procesos automatizados de la banca tradicional, en Kapital cada transferencia de alto volumen puede contar con el acompañamiento de un ejecutivo. Esto permite elegir el momento de mayor estabilidad cambiaria, protegiendo la rentabilidad de la operación. Empresas aptas para operar cambio de divisas La infraestructura de Kapital FX está diseñada para impulsar el crecimiento de una amplia gama de perfiles empresariales. El acceso es total para aquellas organizaciones que buscan una gestión de cambio de divisas profesional y transparente. El servicio de Kapital FX está disponible para empresas nacionales y extranjeras con visión de expansión que requieran movilizar capital internacionalmente. El requisito fundamental es poseer una Cuenta Kapital activa o un Contrato Marco de Divisas formalizado. La seguridad en Kapital FX En el manejo del capital, la seguridad es la prioridad absoluta. Operar con Kapital FX implica el respaldo de un grupo financiero regulado: Respaldo y Regulación Oficial: Kapital opera bajo la estricta supervisión de la CNBV , Banxico y la SHCP . title: Is the Duolingo English Test accepted in Scotland?
summary: Planning to study in Scotland? Discover leading Scottish universities that accept the Duolingo English Test and start planning your next adventure.
body_text: Yes. The Duolingo English Test (DET) is an online English proficiency test accepted by more than 6,500 institutions worldwide. And many universities in Scotland accept the DET as proof of English proficiency for English-taught undergraduate and postgraduate programs. Scotland welcomes international students Scotland has long been a destination for students seeking academic excellence in a welcoming, international environment. Its universities combine world-class teaching with groundbreaking research, while cities like Edinburgh, Glasgow, and Aberdeen each offer their own unique blend of culture and student life. With English-taught undergraduate and postgraduate programs spanning nearly every discipline, Scotland provides students with the opportunity to earn globally recognized degrees while experiencing everything from medieval castles and dramatic coastlines to vibrant arts festivals and innovative technology hubs. Scottish universities that accept the Duolingo English Test The Duolingo English Test is accepted by leading universities throughout Scotland, including: University of St Andrews : Scotland's oldest university and one of the UK's most prestigious institutions, St Andrews is renowned for its academic excellence, close-knit community, and beautiful coastal setting. title: FedEx and Orbis International Team Up to Expand Access to Eye Care in Vietnam
summary: Long-standing FedEx support helps bring the Orbis Flying Eye Hospital to Da Nang for intensive training, knowledge exchange, and technology-enabled learning for eye care professionals across Central Vietnam and the Central Highlands
body_text: Federal Express Corporation (FedEx), one of the world’s largest express transportation companies, today underscored its long-standing support for Orbis International’s work to strengthen eye health systems in Vietnam. Through this collaboration, FedEx helps connect local eye care teams with the global expertise, resources, and learning opportunities needed to build sustainable capacity and expand access to care. The Orbis Flying Eye Hospital has returned to Da Nang for the fifth time to bring together ophthalmologists, residents, anesthesiologists, nurses and biomedical engineers from hospitals across Vietnam for simulation-based learning, surgical mentoring, supervised clinical care, and exchange with international and local Volunteer Faculty over the following two weeks. These activities will provide valuable hands-on learning opportunities for about 230 participating healthcare professionals, building skills that can help expand access to specialized eye care for communities across Central Vietnam and the Central Highlands. The project builds on Orbis’s three decades of collaboration with Vietnam’s eye health community, during which Orbis and local partners have worked together to expand access to care, strengthen institutions, and support the development of local expertise. According to the Ministry of Health, an estimated two million people in Vietnam are living with blindness or vision loss, underscoring the importance of continued investment in professional training and sustainable eye care services nationwide. FedEx has supported the Orbis Flying Eye Hospital by sponsoring the MD-10 aircraft and providing volunteer pilots who help transport the world’s only fully accredited flying ophthalmic teaching hospital to communities around the globe. In Vietnam, this long-standing partnership supports the development of local medical expertise through hands-on training and collaboration, helping improve access to quality eye care long after the Flying Eye Hospital has departed. “At FedEx, we believe that connecting people goes beyond delivering packages – it is about creating opportunities and helping communities thrive,” said Ee-Hui Tan, managing director of FedEx Vietnam and Cambodia. “We are proud to support the return of the Orbis Flying Eye Hospital to Vietnam. Together with Orbis, we are investing in the knowledge and skills of healthcare professionals, helping strengthen Vietnam’s eye care system so more patients can access quality care closer to home.” The Orbis Flying Eye Hospital is a state-of-the-art, fully converted aircraft equipped with an ophthalmic teaching facility. This project in Da Nang is part of Orbis’s broader model for creating lasting change: investing in people, institutions, technology, and local leadership. Cybersight, Orbis’s telemedicine and e-learning platform, is integrated into the project to help participants prepare in advance, consult with global experts, access ongoing education, and continue building skills after the in-person training concludes. Vietnam is emerging as a regional leader in eye health, with growing strengths in pediatric care, diabetic retinopathy, retinopathy of prematurity, workforce development, and technology-enabled care. By supporting the Flying Eye Hospital, FedEx helps Orbis and Vietnamese partners accelerate progress that is locally led and designed to continue beyond any single project. “This project is the latest chapter in a long-term partnership to advance Vietnam’s eye health system,” said Kathleen Sherwin, President & CEO, Orbis International. “FedEx’s support helps make the Flying Eye Hospital possible—bringing intensive, hands-on training together with tools like Cybersight so local teams can continue improving care long after the project ends. We are grateful for FedEx’s commitment to helping Orbis support local leadership and expand access to quality eye care.” Today’s opening ceremony marks another milestone in the long-standing collaboration between FedEx, Orbis, and partners in Vietnam. By helping bring the Flying Eye Hospital to Da Nang, FedEx is supporting a model of training and innovation that strengthens local skills, fosters collaboration and helps build a more resilient, sustainable eye care system that will benefit communities across the country for years to come.

title: CTS Unveils New Pushbutton Switch
body_text: CTS Corporation (NYSE: CTS) is launching a new product line in shape of the series 229 pushbutton switch . Pushbutton switches, also known as 'key switches', are mechanical devices used for initiation and breaking of a circuit. The series 229 pushbutton switch is the first of its kind in the CTS product portfolio, intended for use in applications that operate in harsh environments where standard tactile switches would not suffice. With a robust internal structure and an optional IP67 rating, the series 229 pushbutton switch is well-equipped to handle the wear and tear of outdoor use and dust/humidity exposure. It will help enhance driving controls of transportation two- and three-wheelers as well as off-road vehicles, in addition to providing first-class circuit control for a range of industrial applications. title: FlexAir™: A Breakthrough in Sustainable Automotive Seating
body_text: Lear’s engineering team set out to design a recyclable, foam-free seating material that could deliver comfort and performance comparable to conventional solutions, while addressing long-term sustainability requirements. The result is FlexAir™, a 100% recyclable, 100% breathable, foam-free alternative that combines advanced polymer science with a unique extrusion process. As the industry’s first extruded 3D loop polyethylene cushioning, FlexAir delivers luxury comfort, durability, and lighter weight — while meeting the rigorous performance standards of modern vehicles. By integrating air, polyethylene loops, and Lear’s materials expertise, FlexAir establishes a new benchmark for seating innovation with both commercial and environmental benefits. Through an innovative design and production process, FlexAir combines air, advanced polymer science, and Lear’s seating expertise to achieve a technology that is lighter in weight and engineered to meet the rigorous performance standards of modern vehicles. Innovation Backed by Science ‍ FlexAir is more than a chemistry change or subtle shift in processes. It’s a transformation powered by: More than 450 patents, protecting innovations across comfort, durability, environment and recycling qualities. A water-based extrusion process that produces resilient, lightweight loops engineered for long-term comfort. Provides up to 20% weight reduction and improved durability compared to traditional materials Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) emissions below 1% compared to traditional materials, creating a safer work environment for employees Sustainability with Proof ‍ FlexAir is 100% recyclable — a true foam-free alternative that reduces CO₂ emissions by up to 50% compared to traditional seat cushion materials. This innovation has the potential to divert up to 2.5 billion pounds of waste annually from landfills. By eliminating liquid resins and enabling circularity through solid pellets, FlexAir supports a cradle-to-cradle lifecycle for seating materials. ‍ Partnership Power ‍ This breakthrough was made possible through Lear’s seating expertise and a partnership with Dow MobilityScience , which together advanced the material architecture and processing required to meet stringent automotive standards. ‍ On the Road & Scaling Fast ‍ As automakers set ambitious goals for carbon reduction and recyclability, innovations like FlexAir will play an increasingly important role. With commercial applications already underway and multiple global OEM programs in development, FlexAir represents a step forward in aligning seating technology with the mobility industry’s objectives.

title: Duke Energy Florida delivers $50 million in customer savings, avoids 2027 base rate increase through innovative tax strategy
summary: Duke Energy Florida is delivering $50 million in customer savings in 2027.
body_text: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – Duke Energy Florida is delivering $50 million in customer savings in 2027. The company is implementing an innovative strategy to accelerate the return of tax credits over one year rather than the standard 15-year lifespan of its Powerline Battery Energy Storage System. This will avoid the 2% base rate increase outlined in its multiyear (2025-2027) rate agreement and help keep costs as low as possible for customers. Our view “Our customers count on us to continually look for ways to keep our costs in check and help ease their overall financial burden – especially as prices continue to rise in seemingly every aspect of our daily lives,” said Melissa Seixas, Duke Energy Florida state president. “By finding a way to return these tax credits faster, we’re able to put millions of dollars to work for our customers sooner, while also building the modern energy infrastructure Florida’s rapidly growing communities need.” Better reliability, more savings Over the next 10 years, Duke Energy Florida plans to build 1.4 gigawatts of battery storage, which will result in more than $500 million in investment tax credits that the company will pass on directly to customers. Batteries play an important role in Duke Energy Florida’s “all-of-the-above” approach to power generation, storing electricity when demand is low and making it available when customers need it most. The company currently has six sites located throughout the state; the Powerline Battery Energy Storage System in Citrus County will be the seventh site when it is completed next year. The more batteries Duke Energy Florida adds to its portfolio, the more useful solar energy sites become, as customers can benefit from the stored energy even when it is cloudy or the sun has gone down. The company is working to establish 12 new solar energy sites by the end of 2028, saving customers a total of approximately $3 billion in displaced fuel costs throughout their service lifetimes. In 2025, the company passed on approximately $65 million in production tax credits from solar energy sites to customers – an amount that will grow as more sites are completed – reducing residential rates by at least $2.50 per 1,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity used. Need help now? While Duke Energy Florida lowered residential customers’ rates three times in 2026 and continues to look for new, creative ways to provide relief, the company understands energy use – and bills – may be surging as temperatures rise this summer. Customers are encouraged to take advantage of the many energy efficiency and financial assistance programs available to them, from free assessments of their home’s energy use to flexible payment plans. For more information, please visit duke-energy.com/SummerSolutions . Duke Energy Florida Duke Energy Florida, a subsidiary of Duke Energy, owns 12,500 megawatts of energy capacity, supplying electricity to 2 million residential, commercial and industrial customers across a 13,000-square-mile service area in Florida. Duke Energy Duke Energy (NYSE: DUK), a Fortune 150 company headquartered in Charlotte, N.C., is one of America’s largest energy holding companies. The company’s electric utilities serve 8.7 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky, and collectively own 55,700 megawatts of energy capacity. Its natural gas utilities serve 1.6 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio and Kentucky. Duke Energy is executing an energy modernization strategy, keeping customer value at the forefront as it invests in electric grid upgrades and efficient generation resources to strengthen the system and serve growing energy needs. More information is available at duke-energy.com . Follow Duke Energy on X, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook for stories about the people and innovations powering its communities. body_text: A few years ago, Gartner published its last Magic Quadrant for ITSM, a signal that the market had settled into a familiar set of features, in our view. Since that time, the category has evolved. AI has reset what employees expect from service, infrastructure is harder to see and govern, and service management is no longer just about managing tickets—it requires deep infrastructure and asset context to drive reliable outcomes. That's why the return of the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for IT Service Management Platforms matters, and why we're proud to share that Freshworks has been named a Leader. We believe this recognition reflects our commitment to building Freshservice into an AI-powered, unified service operations platform for agile enterprises—organizations that need depth, governance, and scale without the operational drag of legacy platforms. Companies like New Balance , Amerisure , and the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team already trust Freshservice to run that way. Our customer base experiences a CSAT of 97.8% and an average first contact resolution of 75%. Freshworks' domain-specific AI increases agent productivity by 40% while deflecting more than 65% of employee queries ( Freshservice Benchmark Report, 2025 ). Delivering these outcomes requires more than just a faster help desk. The old service model—something happens, a ticket opens, a human responds—breaks down the moment teams juggle distributed assets, major incidents, and rising demand for AI-powered support. Our strategy rests on three bets: Unified service ops platform: Services, assets, incidents, and knowledge connected on a single platform with a common data and context model, eliminating silos and providing the rich context legacy systems lack. Trusted, domain-specific AI: Deploys intelligent agents across critical workflows—including IT and HR requests, incident triage, and multichannel self-service—to automate routine resolutions while maintaining policy guardrails. Rapid impact: Short implementation cycles that deliver value fast: 80% of customers go live in under 90 days, with 168% ROI and a six-month payback ( Futurum Business Economic Value Report ). We believe this recognition reinforces our commitment to our 20,000+ customers. We'll keep turning your feedback into monthly releases, so the platform keeps evolving around how you actually work. And we'll hold to one principle as we do: automate what can be automated, keep human judgment where it matters, and give you the visibility and control to scale with confidence. That's the platform we're building. To our customers, partners, and Freshworks teams: Thank you. We're just getting started.
